title: Alternation: this or that
explanation:
The pipe `|` means **or**: `/green|red/` matches "green" or "red". Each side is called an *alternative*, and the engine tries them from left to right at each position.

`|` has the **lowest precedence** of all regex operators — it splits the *entire* pattern (or the enclosing group) into alternatives. That is convenient for multi-character words (`Crow|Servo` means "Crow" or "Servo", not "Cro" + ("w" or "S") + "ervo"), but it surprises people when anchors are involved: `^yes|no$` means "`yes` at the start" **or** "`no` at the end", so it accepts `"yesterday"`.

```js
console.log(/^yes|no$/.test("yesterday"));     // true  -- only the first alternative needed to match
console.log(/^(?:yes|no)$/.test("yesterday")); // false -- group the alternatives, then anchor
console.log(/^(?:yes|no)$/.test("no"));        // true
```

So: wrap alternatives in a group — usually non-capturing `(?:...)` — whenever they share surrounding pattern such as anchors or a common prefix/suffix. And if the alternatives are single characters, a character class (`[abc]`) is simpler than `a|b|c`.
keyIdeas: `|` has the lowest precedence: it splits the whole pattern or group.
Group alternatives with `(?:...)` before anchoring or adding context.
For single characters, prefer a class `[abc]`.

workedExample.problem: Accept image file names made of letters, digits, `_` or `-`, ending in `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, or `.png`. Accept `"cat.jpg"`, `"my-photo.jpeg"`, `"logo_2.png"`; reject `"notes.txt"`, `"image.png.exe"`, and `".png"`.
steps: The name part is one or more allowed characters: `[\w-]+`.
The extensions are alternatives that share the same position after a literal dot: `\.(?:jpe?g|png)` — `jpe?g` covers both jpg and jpeg.
Anchor the whole thing, with the group keeping `^` and `$` outside the alternation: `^[\w-]+\.(?:jpe?g|png)$`.
workedExample.answer: `/^[\w-]+\.(?:jpe?g|png)$/`. Without the group, `^[\w-]+\.jpe?g|png$` would accept anything that merely ends in `png`, such as `"x.txtpng"`.

pitfalls: Anchoring ungrouped alternatives (`^a|b$`) and accidentally anchoring only the first and last alternative.
Using a capturing group for alternation and shifting the numbers of later captures.
Ordering alternatives so a shorter one wins first (`/in|int/` finds `in` inside `"int"`).

citations.quote: Disjunction: Matches either "x" or "y". Each component, separated by a pipe (|), is called an alternative.
| has very low precedence in order to make it work reasonably when you're alternating multi-character strings. Crow|Servo will match either 'Crow' or 'Servo'
Non-capturing group: Matches "x" but does not remember the match.
Note: A disjunction is another way to specify "a set of choices"
